value.body: Software developers write, test and maintain the code behind applications, websites and systems. They work in IT services firms, product companies, startups and in-house tech teams of banks and other businesses, and the day mixes coding, reviewing code, fixing bugs and meetings with the team.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech / B.E., BCA, B.Sc Computer Science, MCA

items.label: Common tools
items.value: A programming language (Java, Python, JavaScript…), Git, SQL

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most freshers enter through campus placement or off-campus drives at IT services firms, which run aptitude and coding tests and then a training period. Product companies and startups hire more on coding tests and projects, so a portfolio of work on Git helps.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Programming in at least one language

value.title: At a glance
items: Entry-level hiring volume varies a lot from year to year.
Common next steps: senior developer, tech lead, architect, or a move into product or DevOps.
Tools change fast, so ongoing learning is part of the job.
